result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_min_cut_between()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get minimum cut between source and sink nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25561-L25618){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_min_cut_between( source, sink, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Minimum cut between two nodes](/assets/graphs/get-min-cut-between.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two diamonds that share the hub node D, with B and E outlined as source and sink. The two accent edges B–D and C–D are a smallest set of edges whose removal separates B from E. The card shows that cut and its size 2." width="100%"} Computes the minimum number of edges that must be removed to disconnect the source from the sink. Uses the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm with BFS (Edmonds-Karp) to find maximum flow, which equals the minimum cut by the max-flow min-cut theorem. For unweighted graphs, each edge has capacity `1`. For undirected graphs, edges are treated as bidirectional. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (integer ID or string label). [sink]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sink node (integer ID or string label). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Size of minimum cut (number of edges to remove). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or sink node doesn't exist, or if they're the same. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a simple path-like graph, the single edge in the middle is the bottleneck, so the minimum cut is just 1: ::: {#ee3389db .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B", auto_create_nodes=True) .add_edge("B", "C", auto_create_nodes=True) .add_edge("C", "D", auto_create_nodes=True) ) a_id, d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A"), graph.get_id_from_label("D") # Returns 1 (bottleneck) graph.get_min_cut_between(a_id, d_id) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: :::
